intent.raw_query: Portugal Algarve, $2200, beach holiday with wine tasting, September 2026 from London

selected_hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Cliff Walk & Snorkeling
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, known for its dramatic golden limestone cliffs and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Hike the scenic coastal trail and snorkel among sea caves and rock arches teeming with marine life.

experiences.name: Algarve Beachfront Wine & Seafood Tasting
experiences.description: Join a curated tasting session at a beachfront restaurant in Albufeira featuring local Algarve wines such as Vida Nova rosé and Quinta dos Vales red, paired with fresh grilled sardines, percebes, and regional petiscos with ocean views.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle through the iconic Benagil sea cave, one of the most photographed natural wonders in Portugal. A guided kayak tour takes you through hidden grottos, arched rock formations, and secluded beaches accessible only by water.

experiences.name: Quinta dos Vales Vineyard & Wine Tour
experiences.description: Visit one of the Algarve's premier inland-coastal wineries for a guided tour of the vineyards and wine cellar, followed by a tasting of award-winning reds, whites, and rosés. The estate also features stunning sculpture gardens and panoramic countryside views.
experiences.location: Quinta dos Vales, Estômbar near Lagoa

experiences.name: Meia Praia Sunset Beach Horseback Ride
experiences.description: Ride along the longest and most pristine stretch of beach in the Algarve as the sun sets over the Atlantic. This guided horseback experience is perfect for all skill levels and offers breathtaking golden-hour views along the shoreline near Lagos.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Portugal Algarve
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrives at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Collect luggage, clear customs, and arrange transfer to Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay (approx. 1 hour drive from Faro Airport). Consider pre-booking a shared shuttle or taking the bus to Lagoa for budget savings (~€5–10 vs €50+ taxi).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in, freshen up, then take a short 10-minute walk to the iconic Praia da Marinha beach. Explore the dramatic golden limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear waters. No entrance fee — just bring sunscreen and enjoy the scenery. Pick up groceries at a local mini-market (Intermarché in Lagoa, ~5km) for snacks and breakfast supplies.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the coastal clifftop path near Praia da Marinha at sunset for stunning views. Head back and have a relaxed first evening settling in.

meals.breakfast: Grab a pastel de nata and coffee at the airport or a café near arrivals (~€2–3)
meals.lunch: Snack on packed food from airport or grab a bifana (pork sandwich) at a local café near Lagoa town for ~€3–4
meals.dinner: Self-catering at the accommodation using groceries from the local mini-market — simple pasta, local cheese, bread, and wine (~€8–10 total)

day_by_day.notes: September in the Algarve is warm (avg 25–28°C) with fewer crowds than peak summer. Exchange some euros before arrival or use ATMs in Faro. Keep receipts for budget tracking.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning swim and exploration at Praia da Marinha — arrive before 9am to enjoy the beach almost to yourself. Walk the coastal trail eastward toward Praia do Carvalho (30-min walk). These hidden cove beaches are free and spectacular.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle in Lagoa town (~€10–15/day) and cycle to Benagil Cave viewpoint (approx. 5km). Take a kayak tour from Praia de Benagil to enter the famous Benagil Sea Cave (budget operators charge ~€10–15 per person for a group kayak). Book in advance online for best prices.
day_by_day.evening: Return bikes and head to Lagoa town center. Visit the local market area and explore the charming whitewashed streets.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation — local bread, fruit, yogurt, and coffee (~€2–3)
meals.lunch: Grab a fresh grilled sardine sandwich or prego roll from a beach snack bar near Benagil (~€4–6)
meals.dinner: Dine at a local tasca (traditional tavern) in Lagoa — look for prato do dia (dish of the day) which typically includes soup, main, and drink for ~€8–12. Try Restaurante O Alambique in Lagoa.

day_by_day.notes: Book Benagil kayak tour the evening before as spots fill quickly even in September. Wear water shoes for rocky cove beaches.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Praia de Albandeira and Praia da Corredoura — two secluded beaches a short drive or long clifftop walk from Praia da Marinha. These are less visited gems with dramatic rock arches. Pack a picnic from the morning market.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head inland to Lagoa town and visit the Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa — one of the Algarve's oldest wine cooperatives offering free or very low-cost cellar tours and tastings of local wines including the famous Lagoa DOC wines (~€2–5 for tasting). Call ahead to confirm opening times.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks with a bottle of local Lagoa wine purchased at the cooperative (~€5–8/bottle) enjoyed on the clifftops near the accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — scrambled eggs, local bread, and coffee (~€2–3)
meals.lunch: Picnic on the beach — local cheese, presunto (cured ham), olives, bread, and fruit from the market (~€6–8)
meals.dinner: Cook at accommodation — grilled local fish (pick up fresh at the market) with vegetables and rice (~€10–12 for two)

day_by_day.notes: Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa is a hidden gem for budget wine lovers — their table wines are excellent value. Confirm opening hours as they vary seasonally.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Silves — take the local bus from Lagoa (Rede Expressos or local Proximo bus, ~€2–3 each way). Visit the impressive Silves Castle (Castelo de Silves), a Moorish red sandstone fortress with panoramic views. Entry ~€3 with discounts available.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Silves old town — walk the medieval walls, visit the Gothic Silves Cathedral (free entry), and browse the weekly market if visiting on a market day. Silves is also the heart of Algarve citrus and almond country.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagoa by bus and enjoy a Friday evening passeio (evening stroll) in Lagoa town. Check out any local events or live music in the main square.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and pastel de nata at a café in Lagoa before catching the bus (~€2)
meals.lunch: Lunch in Silves at Café Inglês or a local tasca — cataplana de peixe (fish stew) or grilled chicken with fries for ~€8–10
meals.dinner: Budget pizza or local sandwich at a café near accommodation (~€6–8)

day_by_day.notes: Silves Castle is one of the best-preserved Moorish castles in Portugal — not to be missed. The town is quieter and more authentic than the coastal resorts. Check bus timetables in advance at rede-expressos.pt.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at Praia da Marinha — September weekends can be busier so arrive early. Try snorkeling in the clear waters around the rock formations (bring or rent snorkel gear from a local shop ~€5–8).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Carvoeiro village (5km from accommodation, accessible by taxi ~€8 or bicycle). Explore the charming fishing village, the Algar Seco rock formations (free, spectacular), and the tiny Carvoeiro beach. Browse local artisan shops for affordable souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the lively Saturday atmosphere in Carvoeiro — have drinks at a clifftop bar watching the sunset. Return to accommodation by taxi or arrange a ride.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — local yogurt with honey and almonds, coffee (~€2–3)
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood at a simple restaurant in Carvoeiro — grilled fish of the day with salad for ~€10–13
meals.dinner: Self-catered barbecue at accommodation if facilities available — local sausages, vegetables, and bread (~€8–10) with a bottle of Lagoa wine

day_by_day.notes: Algar Seco in Carvoeiro is free to visit and rivals any paid attraction. The rock formations at low tide are extraordinary. Check tide times for best access.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed Sunday morning — sleep in, enjoy a slow breakfast, then take a long clifftop hike on the Percurso dos Sete Vales Suspensos (Seven Hanging Valleys Trail). This is one of Portugal's most beautiful coastal walks, starting from Praia de Vale Centeanes to Praia da Marinha. Completely free, ~6km, 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Post-hike swim and relaxation at Praia da Marinha. Hire a SUP board or kayak from a beach vendor (~€10–15/hour) to explore the sea caves from the water.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the local Sunday market in Lagoa (if running) for fresh produce, local honey, almonds, and handicrafts. Perfect for picking up affordable gifts.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — large breakfast before the hike: eggs, toast, fruit, coffee (~€3–4)
meals.lunch: Pack a trail lunch — sandwiches, fruit, nuts, and water (~€4–5)
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to a slightly nicer Sunday dinner at a local restaurant — try bacalhau à brás (salted cod with eggs and potatoes) for ~€10–12 at a local tasca in Lagoa

day_by_day.notes: The Seven Hanging Valleys Trail is a must-do — wear sturdy shoes and bring plenty of water. The trail can be hot in September so start early. Download the trail map offline at wikiloc.com.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Portimão — take the local bus (~€2–3). Visit the Museu de Portimão, an excellent free museum (or ~€3 entry) housed in a former sardine cannery documenting the Algarve's fishing heritage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk across the bridge to Ferragudo — a beautifully preserved fishing village with a castle (Castelo de São João do Arade) and charming cobblestone streets. Completely free to wander. Praia Grande de Ferragudo is a lovely beach for a swim.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Portimão for dinner along the riverside — the Portimão riverside restaurants are famous for grilled sardines and are generally good value. Return to accommodation by bus.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and toast at a café in Lagoa before the bus (~€2–3)
meals.lunch: Grilled sardines with bread and salad at a riverside café in Portimão — a Portuguese classic for ~€7–9
meals.dinner: Grilled chicken (frango grelhado) or bifanas at a local tasca in Portimão before the return bus (~€7–10)

day_by_day.notes: Ferragudo is often overlooked by tourists but is one of the most authentic and beautiful villages in the Algarve. The contrast with busy Portimão makes it even more special.

day_by_day.morning: Morning wine tasting experience — visit Quinta dos Vales winery near Estômbar (approx. 10km from accommodation, taxi ~€15 or arrange a wine tour shuttle). They offer guided tours and tastings of award-winning Algarve wines for ~€10–15 per person. Book in advance.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the winery, stop at Estômbar village for a walk along the Arade River. Alternatively, visit the Silves region vineyards on a self-guided cycling route if you prefer to stay on two wheels.
day_by_day.evening: Return to accommodation. Cook a special dinner pairing wines purchased at the winery with local cheeses, charcuterie, and bread from the market.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — light breakfast before the winery visit (~€2–3)
meals.lunch: Many wineries offer light lunch platters with the tasting — or pack a picnic to enjoy on the winery grounds (~€6–8)
meals.dinner: Wine and cheese board at accommodation with winery purchases (~€10–15 total)

day_by_day.notes: Quinta dos Vales is one of the most visitor-friendly wineries in the Algarve. Alternatively, Quinta do Barranco Longo near Porches is another excellent budget-friendly option. Pre-booking is essential.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Lagos — take the train from Tunes or bus from Portimão (~€4–6). Visit Ponta da Piedade, the most dramatic rock formation coastline in the Algarve. Hire a small boat tour from Lagos marina (~€10–15) to see the grottos and arches up close.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Lagos old town — walk the historic city walls, visit Igreja de Santo António (small entry fee ~€2), and browse the colorful streets. Praia Dona Ana and Praia do Camilo are beautiful beaches within walking distance of town.
day_by_day.evening: Evening in Lagos — enjoy the vibrant Wednesday evening atmosphere, grab a drink at a rooftop bar, and return by bus or train to Lagoa.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and pastel de nata at a café in Lagoa before departure (~€2)
meals.lunch: Lunch in Lagos — piri-piri chicken at a local restaurant or a fresh tuna steak for ~€10–12
meals.dinner: Affordable dinner in Lagos before return — try a local petiscos (tapas-style) bar for a variety of small dishes at ~€10–13

day_by_day.notes: Lagos is easily one of the highlights of the Algarve — the combination of history, beaches, and nightlife is unmatched. The boat tour from the marina to Ponta da Piedade grottos is worth every cent.

day_by_day.morning: Slow morning at Praia da Marinha — enjoy what may be one of your last uncrowded beach mornings. Take photographs of the cliffs in the soft morning light. Journal, read, or simply relax.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Porches Pottery (Olaria Algarve) near Porches village (~8km from accommodation). This is the Algarve's most famous azulejo (hand-painted tile) workshop. Browsing is free and small tiles make affordable, authentic souvenirs (~€5–15). Watch artisans at work.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Praia da Marinha followed by a farewell-style dinner at a local restaurant in Lagoa.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — full Portuguese-style breakfast at accommodation (~€3–4)
meals.lunch: Picnic on the beach or light snack at a café near Porches (~€5–7)
meals.dinner: Local tasca in Lagoa — try açorda de marisco (seafood bread stew) or grilled dourada (sea bream) for ~€10–13

day_by_day.notes: Porches Pottery is a wonderful and free cultural experience. The hand-painted ceramics are genuinely made on-site and make meaningful, lightweight souvenirs. Pick up a few small tiles as gifts.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Faro — take the bus from Lagoa (~€6–8 return). Explore the Faro Old Town (Cidade Velha) — walk through the Arco da Vila, visit the Faro Cathedral (Torre da Sé) for panoramic views (~€3.50), and wander the atmospheric cobblestone streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a ferry from Faro marina to Ilha Deserta (Desert Island) in the Ria Formosa Natural Park (~€10 return) — a stunning uninhabited barrier island with pristine beaches and clear lagoon waters. Perfect for a September afternoon swim.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Faro for a waterfront evening stroll and dinner before the bus back to Lagoa.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and tosta mista (toasted ham and cheese sandwich) at a café before the bus (~€3)
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic for Ilha Deserta — or grab food at the island's only restaurant (slightly pricier, ~€12–15)
meals.dinner: Dinner in Faro before the return bus — local restaurant near the marina for grilled fish or cataplana for ~€10–13

day_by_day.notes: The Ria Formosa Natural Park is a UNESCO-listed lagoon system and one of Portugal's 7 Natural Wonders. Ilha Deserta in September is magical with warm water and very few visitors. Check ferry timetables at animaris.pt.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach morning — return to Praia da Marinha for a long, leisurely swim and cliff walk. Take time to appreciate the incredible natural beauty of this UNESCO-protected coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Saturday market in Lagoa or nearby Portimão for last-minute shopping — local almonds, figs, carob products, honey, and wine make excellent affordable gifts. Pack purchases carefully for the return flight.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner — splurge slightly on a memorable final dinner. Try a seafood cataplana (traditional copper pot seafood stew) at a local restaurant — a true Algarve culinary experience. Budget ~€15–18 for this special meal.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — use up remaining groceries for a hearty final breakfast (~€3–4)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the market — fresh fruit, local cheese, and bread (~€5–6)
meals.dinner: Farewell cataplana dinner at a local restaurant in Lagoa or Carvoeiro — worth the slight splurge at ~€15–18 per person. Pair with a glass of local Lagoa DOC wine.

day_by_day.notes: A cataplana is the signature dish of the Algarve and the perfect way to end the trip. Many restaurants require 24-hour advance notice to prepare it, so book ahead. Pack bags tonight to make morning departure stress-free.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — check out of Lagoa Boutique Stay. Take one last walk to the Praia da Marinha clifftop viewpoint for a final look at the stunning coastline. Transfer to Faro Airport for departure (allow 1.5–2 hours including transfer time). Pre-book a shared shuttle for budget savings (~€10–15 vs €50+ taxi).
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure from Faro Airport. Browse duty-free for any last-minute Portuguese wine, pastries, or port wine at airport prices.
day_by_day.evening: Flight home — carry memories of 13 incredible days in one of Europe's most beautiful coastlines.

meals.breakfast: Final pastel de nata and galão (milky coffee) at a café in Lagoa before checkout (~€3)
meals.lunch: Airport café or pack remaining snacks from accommodation (~€5–8)
meals.dinner: Inflight or at home

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary estimate for 13 days per person: Accommodation (pre-booked), Local transport ~€60–80, Activities & entrance fees ~€60–80, Food & drink ~€150–180, Souvenirs & shopping ~€30–50. Total estimated spend excluding flights and accommodation: ~€300–390 per person. September is ideal — warm weather, lower prices than July/August, and fewer crowds.

trip_options.title: Classic Portugal Algarve Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Faro Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Collect luggage, pick up a rental car (highly recommended for Algarve exploration), and drive ~45 minutes west to Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your room.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a gentle first walk down to Praia da Marinha beach (a short walk from the hotel). This stunning cove with golden limestone cliffs and crystal-clear turquoise water is one of Portugal's most iconic beaches. Swim, relax on the sand, and soak in your first Algarve sunset views from the clifftop trail.
day_by_day.evening: Head into the nearby village of Carvoeiro (10-minute drive) for a relaxed first dinner. Stroll the charming main square and beachfront promenade before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Grab a pastel de nata and coffee at the airport or a café near the hotel upon arrival
meals.lunch: Light snack at the hotel or a café in Lagoa town on the way from the airport
meals.dinner: O Castelo Restaurant in Carvoeiro — mid-range Portuguese seafood and grilled fish with ocean views (€20–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Rent a car at Faro Airport for the full trip — essential for exploring the Algarve. September is ideal: warm (26–28°C), less crowded than August, and the sea is still warm. Keep Day 1 light to recover from travel.

day_by_day.morning: After a proper Portuguese breakfast at the hotel, drive 20 minutes west to explore the Benagil Sea Cave — one of the Algarve's most spectacular natural wonders. Book a kayak tour or stand-up paddleboard excursion from Benagil Beach (depart ~9:30 AM before crowds build). Paddle through sea arches and into the famous cathedral cave.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue west along the coast to Praia do Carvalho and Praia de Albandeira — two hidden cove beaches accessible via short cliff walks. Spend the afternoon swimming and snorkeling in calm September waters. Pack a light picnic or stop at a beach kiosk.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Carvoeiro village for the evening. Browse the local shops and enjoy sundowners at a clifftop bar before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full Portuguese breakfast at the boutique hotel — bread, cheese, ham, fruit, coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic on the beach with local bread, cheese, olives, and fruit from a Lagoa supermarket, or a beach kiosk snack
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Escondidinho in Carvoeiro — traditional Algarvian cataplana (seafood stew) and local wine (€22–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Benagil kayak tour in advance online — spots fill up quickly even in September. Start the paddle early (before 10 AM) to avoid crowds inside the cave. Wear water shoes and bring reef-safe sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Drive 30 minutes east to Silves — the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve. Visit the impressive red sandstone Castelo de Silves (€3 entry), walk the medieval ramparts, and explore the Cathedral of Silves. The town is quiet and atmospheric in September.
day_by_day.afternoon: After exploring Silves, head to the Silves wine region. Visit Quinta dos Vales winery (~15 minutes from Silves) for a guided vineyard tour and wine tasting session. The estate produces excellent Algarve reds and whites. Book ahead for a tasting of 4–6 wines paired with local charcuterie (€15–25 per person).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Lagoa/Carvoeiro area. Have a relaxed dinner in Lagoa town, the heart of Algarve wine country.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Café Inglês in Silves — a charming mid-range restaurant inside the castle walls serving light lunches and salads (€12–18 per person)
meals.dinner: Tasca do Zé in Lagoa — a beloved local tasca with daily specials, piri-piri chicken, and local Lagoa wine (€15–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Silves is best visited in the morning before the heat peaks. The Silves Medieval Fair has already passed (usually August), but the town is beautifully calm in September. Quinta dos Vales requires advance booking for tours.

day_by_day.morning: Drive 45 minutes west to Lagos — one of the Algarve's most vibrant historic towns. Explore the old town: walk the ancient city walls, visit the Igreja de Santo António (stunning gilded baroque interior), and the Slave Market Museum (Mercado de Escravos) — the first in the world.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Ponta da Piedade headland just south of Lagos — a breathtaking series of golden rock towers, grottos, and sea arches. Walk the clifftop trail (free) for panoramic views, or take a 45-minute boat tour from Lagos Marina to explore the sea caves and grottoes from below (€15–20 per person).
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Lagos for dinner and evening drinks. The town has a lively but relaxed September atmosphere with excellent restaurants and bars.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast, then a coffee and pastel de nata at a Lagos café upon arrival
meals.lunch: A Forja restaurant in Lagos — a local favourite for grilled fish and meat dishes at honest prices (€15–25 per person)
meals.dinner: No Pátio restaurant in Lagos old town — Mediterranean and Portuguese fusion in a lovely courtyard setting (€25–40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Lagos is about 45 minutes from the hotel — park near the marina or old town. The Ponta da Piedade boat tours run until late afternoon; aim for the 3–4 PM slot for golden afternoon light on the rocks.

day_by_day.morning: Drive 1 hour west to Sagres — Portugal's dramatic southwestern tip. Visit the Fortaleza de Sagres (€3 entry), a 15th-century fortress on a windswept promontory where Henry the Navigator planned Portugal's Age of Discovery. Walk the clifftops and look for dolphins in the Atlantic below.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive 10 minutes north to Cabo de São Vicente — the most southwestern point of continental Europe. Stand at the edge of the known world on dramatic 70-metre cliffs. Then head to Praia do Beliche or Praia da Mareta in Sagres for a late afternoon swim in wilder, more rugged Atlantic waters.
day_by_day.evening: Return toward Lagos or drive back toward Carvoeiro. Stop in the small town of Vila do Bispo for dinner on the way back.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast (early start recommended)
meals.lunch: Restaurante O Telheiro do Infante in Sagres — fresh fish and seafood with Atlantic views (€18–30 per person)
meals.dinner: A Eira do Mel in Vila do Bispo — a rustic, highly regarded restaurant known for excellent cataplana and local produce (€20–35 per person); book ahead

day_by_day.notes: Sagres can be windy even in September — bring a light layer. The drive from Praia da Marinha to Sagres is about 1 hour 10 minutes. This is a full day trip, so an early start is recommended. Cabo de São Vicente sunsets are legendary — time your visit accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recharge day. Spend the morning at your home beach — Praia da Marinha. September mornings here are magical with golden light on the limestone cliffs. Take the coastal walking trail along the Percurso dos Sete Vales Suspensos (Seven Hanging Valleys Trail) — a stunning 5.7km clifftop walk east toward Armação de Pêra.
day_by_day.afternoon: Finish the Seven Hanging Valleys Trail or turn back midway. Return to the hotel for a pool afternoon. Alternatively, drive 10 minutes to Praia de Vale Centeanes or Praia do Carvalho for a quieter Sunday swim.
day_by_day.evening: Drive into Portimão (20 minutes) for a Sunday evening market browse and dinner along the riverside.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic for the clifftop walk — local bread, local cheese (queijo), olives, tomatoes, and Algarve almonds from a local market
meals.dinner: Taberna da Maré in Portimão — riverside location, excellent grilled sardines and local wines (€18–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Seven Hanging Valleys Trail is one of the most beautiful coastal walks in Europe. Wear sturdy shoes and bring water. The trail is well-marked. Sunday in September is quiet — perfect for a peaceful clifftop walk with fewer tourists.

day_by_day.morning: Drive 25 minutes to Portimão and take a boat trip up the Arade River to Silves (approximately 1.5–2 hours each way). The river cruise passes through wetlands, citrus groves, and traditional fishing villages — a wonderful perspective of the Algarve interior. Depart from Portimão Marina.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Silves by boat and spend the afternoon revisiting the castle from a different angle, or explore the local ceramic and cork workshops. Visit the Museu Municipal de Arqueologia. Take the return boat back to Portimão in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Portimão's waterfront and have dinner in the city — a larger, more local town than the tourist centres.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Lunch in Silves at Café Restaurante Marisqueira Rui — a local institution for seafood rice and grilled fish (€15–25 per person)
meals.dinner: Churrasqueira O Mané in Portimão — beloved local grill house with piri-piri chicken, ribs, and cold Sagres beer (€12–20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Arade River boat trip in advance — operators include Riosul and local marina companies. The round trip takes most of the day. Alternatively, if boat trips aren't running, drive to Monchique mountain village instead for a scenic inland alternative.

day_by_day.morning: Drive 45 minutes east to Albufeira. Visit the old town (Albufeira Velha) in the morning before the day-trippers arrive — the whitewashed streets, fishermen's beach, and clifftop church are charming in the early light. Explore the local market if it's running.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive 20 minutes east of Albufeira to visit Adega do Cantor winery — famously co-owned by Cliff Richard and producing excellent Algarve wines. Take a guided tour and tasting (book ahead, €15–20 per person). Then visit nearby Quinta da Tôr winery for a second tasting if desired.
day_by_day.evening: Return toward the hotel. Stop in the pretty village of Alte — known as the 'prettiest village in the Algarve' — for a brief evening stroll through its flower-draped streets before heading home.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Restaurante A Ruína in Albufeira old town — a dramatic clifftop restaurant built into old ruins with fresh fish and ocean views (€20–35 per person)
meals.dinner: Back near Lagoa — Restaurante Veneza in Lagoa — a solid mid-range local restaurant with traditional Portuguese dishes (€15–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Adega do Cantor (Vida Nova wines) requires advance booking for tours and tastings. Albufeira old town is far more pleasant in the morning before the beach crowds arrive. Alte is a 30-minute inland detour but absolutely worth it.

day_by_day.morning: Drive 1 hour east to Faro — the Algarve's capital and a wonderfully underrated city. Start at the Cidade Velha (old walled city): visit the Sé Cathedral (climb the tower for panoramic views, €3.50), the Renaissance cloister, and the haunting Igreja dos Ossos (Chapel of Bones) inside the Carmo Church.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a ferry from Faro harbour into the Ria Formosa Natural Park — a stunning coastal lagoon system of islands, salt marshes, and tidal flats. Spend 2–3 hours on Ilha Deserta or Ilha de Faro, swimming in calm lagoon waters and walking along pristine beaches backed by dunes.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Faro city before driving back to the hotel (1 hour).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast (early start)
meals.lunch: A picnic on Ilha Deserta, or lunch at the island's only restaurant — Estaminé — an eco-chic seafood restaurant on a deserted island (€25–40 per person, booking essential)
meals.dinner: Tasca do Bica in Faro — a beloved local tasca with daily blackboard specials, excellent grilled fish, and house wine (€15–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Faro is often overlooked by tourists but is genuinely beautiful. The Ria Formosa ferry runs regularly from Faro harbour — buy tickets at the dock. Estaminé on Ilha Deserta is a bucket-list dining experience but requires a reservation well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Drive 1.5 hours east to Tavira — widely considered the most beautiful town in the Algarve. Cross the Roman bridge over the Gilão River, visit the Castelo de Tavira for panoramic views, and explore the 37 churches (try Igreja de Santa Maria do Castelo). The town is elegant, uncrowded, and deeply Portuguese.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the cable car or ferry from Tavira to Ilha de Tavira — a long barrier island with one of the Algarve's finest beaches. The water is calm and warm in September, the beach is wide and uncrowded, and the dune-backed landscape is spectacular. Spend 2–3 hours swimming and relaxing.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Tavira before the drive back — allow 1.5 hours return to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast (early start for the drive)
meals.lunch: Restaurante Aquasul in Tavira — riverside terrace, fresh seafood, and excellent local wines (€20–30 per person)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bica in Tavira — a classic Tavira institution known for ameijoas (clams), fresh fish, and local Alentejo and Algarve wines (€18–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Tavira is the highlight of the eastern Algarve — don't miss it. The drive from Praia da Marinha is 1.5 hours each way, so plan an early start. September is perfect for Tavira — the summer crowds are gone but the weather and sea are still warm.

day_by_day.morning: A dedicated wine day in the Lagoa wine region — right on your doorstep. Visit Adega Cooperativa do Lagoa — the main wine cooperative of the region and one of the oldest in Portugal. Take a cellar tour and taste the distinctive Algarve wines, including the local Negra Mole grape variety (€8–15 for tasting).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a second local producer: Quinta da Penina or Quinta do Francês near Silves for a more boutique estate experience. Then spend the late afternoon at Praia de Benagil or Praia da Marinha — your home beach — for a final luxurious swim in the September sun.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a special dinner — a slightly elevated mid-range splurge to celebrate the penultimate full day.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: A long, leisurely wine-paired lunch at the winery or at a local adega restaurant in Lagoa town — try grilled tuna with local white wine
meals.dinner: Bon Bon Restaurant in Carvoeiro — the Algarve's Michelin-starred restaurant (book well in advance). A tasting menu experience (€80–120 per person) — a worthy splurge for a special evening

day_by_day.notes: Bon Bon in Carvoeiro holds a Michelin star and is just minutes from your hotel — booking months in advance is essential. If unavailable, Vila Lisa in Mexilhoeira Grande is an excellent alternative (also Michelin-starred). The Lagoa wine cooperative is open Monday–Friday; confirm hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Drive 40 minutes north into the Serra de Monchique — the Algarve's green mountain range. Visit the spa town of Caldas de Monchique, a charming 19th-century thermal village tucked in a wooded valley. Walk the shaded paths, taste the famous mineral water, and browse the local medronho (arbutus berry brandy) shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue up to the summit of Fóia (902m) — the highest point in the Algarve — for sweeping views over the entire region, from the coast to the Spanish border on a clear day. Return via Monchique town, visiting the ruined Convento de Nossa Senhora do Desterro and the Friday market stalls (if still running).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the coast for a final Saturday evening in Carvoeiro — enjoy the beach bars, watch the sunset, and have a relaxed farewell dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Restaurante Central in Monchique — a beloved local spot serving hearty mountain food: slow-roasted pork (porco preto), chouriço, and local bread with medronho (€15–22 per person)
meals.dinner: O Castelo or Restaurante Nau in Carvoeiro — fresh grilled fish, local wine, and a beautiful clifftop setting for a farewell dinner (€22–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Monchique is a wonderful contrast to the coastal Algarve — lush, green, and cool. The drive up to Fóia is on narrow mountain roads — take it slowly. Buy a bottle of medronho brandy as a souvenir. September weekends in Carvoeiro are lively but not overwhelming.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — take one last slow walk down to Praia da Marinha. Swim, sit on the rocks, and take in the extraordinary limestone cliffs one final time. Pack up and check out of the boutique hotel. Drive to Lagoa town for a final Portuguese breakfast at a local café.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive back toward Faro Airport (45 minutes). If time allows before your flight, stop at the Faro waterfront for a final coffee and stroll along the marina promenade, or browse the Faro market for last-minute local souvenirs: Algarve wines, local honey, almond sweets (Dom Rodrigos), and dried figs.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Faro Airport. Carry memories of golden cliffs, turquoise coves, and glasses of Lagoa wine.

meals.breakfast: Final pastel de nata and galão (milky coffee) at a local café in Lagoa — a proper Portuguese send-off
meals.lunch: Light lunch near Faro Airport or at the airport — try a bifana (pork sandwich) or a simple prato do dia at a café near the terminal
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 1.5 hours before your flight for the drive from Lagoa to Faro and airport check-in. Return the rental car at the airport — allow extra time for the drop-off process. Pack any Algarve wines in checked luggage carefully. September flights are generally on time. Boa viagem — safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Portugal Algarve Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival — Flight LH lands at Faro Airport at 13:00. No morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from Faro Airport to Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay (approximately 45 minutes). Settle into your boutique suite, unpack, and enjoy a welcome amenity prepared by the property.
day_by_day.afternoon: After check-in, take a leisurely first stroll along the iconic Praia da Marinha cliff-top trail. Marvel at the golden limestone arches, sea stacks, and turquoise coves that make this one of Europe's most photographed coastlines. Descend to the beach for a relaxed first swim in the warm September Atlantic waters.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset aperitivo on your private terrace or the hotel's panoramic terrace with a glass of chilled Alvarinho. Head to dinner at a nearby fine-dining restaurant in Carvoeiro or Lagoa village for a gentle introduction to the Algarve's cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (mid-day arrival)
meals.lunch: Light welcome spread at the boutique stay upon arrival — charcuterie, local cheeses, fresh fruit, and sparkling water provided by the property
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante O Castelo in Carvoeiro — a premium local restaurant celebrated for its fresh Atlantic seafood, grilled sea bass, and regional cataplana dishes. Pair with a local Algarve white wine.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm private airport transfer in advance. Request early check-in if possible given the 13:00 arrival. Keep Day 1 relaxed to recover from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided kayak and sea cave tour departing from Praia da Marinha beach. Paddle through the dramatic grottos, sea arches, and hidden caves unique to this stretch of coastline. A professional guide will narrate the geology and marine life. September waters are calm and warm — ideal conditions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Algar Seco rock formations near Carvoeiro — a surreal landscape of sculpted golden cliffs, natural pools, and sea blowholes. Enjoy a leisurely cliff-walk and photography session. Stop at the famous Boneca do Algar Seco café perched on the rocks for fresh juice and pastéis de nata.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset sailing cruise departing from Portimão Marina. Sail along the Algarve coastline, watching the sun dip below the horizon from the water with chilled Champagne and canapés on board.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay — freshly baked bread, local honey, smoked swordfish, eggs to order, fresh orange juice, and artisan coffee
meals.lunch: Seafood lunch at Restaurante Boneca do Algar Seco — grilled octopus salad, percebes (barnacles), and local white wine overlooking the Atlantic
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Sueste in Ferragudo — a riverside fine-dining gem renowned for whole roasted fish, tiger prawns, and an exceptional Portuguese wine list

day_by_day.notes: Book the kayak tour and sailing cruise at least 48 hours in advance. Bring reef shoes for the Algar Seco walk. Sunset sailing is weather-dependent — confirm on the morning.

day_by_day.morning: Private wine tasting experience at Quinta dos Vales winery in Estômbar (approximately 20 minutes from the hotel). One of the Algarve's most celebrated estates, set among rolling vineyards and dotted with monumental sculptures. Enjoy a guided vineyard walk, cellar tour, and structured tasting of their premium reds, whites, and rosés.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the wine journey with a visit to Adega do Cantor (the winery founded by Sir Cliff Richard) in Guia — a boutique estate producing acclaimed Vida Nova wines. Enjoy a private tasting paired with local charcuterie and cheeses in the vineyard setting.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a private in-room dinner or terrace dinner arranged by the boutique stay — a curated tasting menu featuring Algarvian ingredients paired with wines selected during the day's tastings.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay
meals.lunch: Wine and food pairing lunch at Quinta dos Vales — artisan breads, regional cheeses, cured meats, and olive oils matched to their premium wine portfolio
meals.dinner: Private curated dinner at the boutique stay — cataplana de marisco (seafood cataplana), grilled Iberian pork secreto, and a selection of Algarve wines

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book both winery visits. Request the premium tasting package at Quinta dos Vales which includes their reserve and grand reserve labels. Consider purchasing bottles to enjoy throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente — Portugal's southwestern tip and the most south-westerly point of continental Europe. Visit the dramatic Fortaleza de Sagres, explore the windswept promontory, and stand at the edge of the known world at Cabo de São Vicente lighthouse. The September light here is extraordinary for photography.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming town of Lagos — one of the Algarve's most beautiful historic towns. Walk the old Moorish city walls, visit the Igreja de Santo António (a Baroque masterpiece), and browse the Ponta da Bandeira fortress. Stroll through the cobbled old town streets and discover local artisan shops.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Lagos at one of the town's top fine-dining establishments before a private transfer back to Praia da Marinha.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurante O Dromedário in Sagres — a beloved local spot with spectacular ocean views, serving fresh grilled fish, clams in garlic and white wine, and cold regional beers
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Casinha do Petisco in Lagos — a celebrated fine-dining restaurant with innovative Algarvian cuisine, exceptional seafood, and a carefully curated Portuguese wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: Sagres can be windy even in September — bring a light jacket. The drive from Praia da Marinha to Sagres is approximately 1 hour. Arrange a private driver for the full day for maximum comfort.

day_by_day.morning: Spa morning at the boutique stay or a nearby luxury spa. Book a 90-minute signature treatment — perhaps a warm stone massage or a traditional Algarvian citrus body wrap using locally sourced carob and almond oils. Spend the remaining morning lounging by the pool.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Praia de Benagil — one of the world's most famous sea caves, accessible by a short boat trip from Benagil beach (just 10 minutes from the hotel). Book a private boat to enter the spectacular Algar de Benagil cave, whose domed ceiling opens to the sky. Swim inside the cave and explore the surrounding hidden beaches.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktails at the hotel terrace, followed by a premium dinner in Lagoa town — exploring the local side of Algarvian gastronomy away from the tourist trail.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay
meals.lunch: Light beach lunch at Restaurante Benagil — fresh grilled sardines, piri-piri prawns, and chilled Sagres beer or local rosé at a classic beachside restaurant
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Quatro Águas in Lagoa — a sophisticated local favourite serving traditional Algarvian recipes elevated with premium ingredients and an excellent regional wine list

day_by_day.notes: Book the private Benagil cave boat in advance — September is still busy. Early afternoon visits to the cave tend to have the best natural light filtering through the ceiling opening.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided stand-up paddleboard (SUP) lesson and tour along the Praia da Marinha coastline. September conditions are typically calm and perfect for paddleboarding. Glide past golden cliffs, explore hidden coves, and enjoy the coastline from a unique perspective on the water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Silves — the medieval Moorish capital of the Algarve (approximately 25 minutes inland). Explore the magnificent red sandstone Castelo de Silves, one of the best-preserved Moorish castles in Portugal. Visit the Gothic Cathedral and wander the atmospheric old town streets lined with orange trees.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private Fado performance dinner in Silves or Lagoa — an intimate setting where Portugal's soulful national music is performed live alongside a premium dinner.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café Inglês in Silves — a charming restaurant within the castle walls serving regional specialities including orange and almond cake (a Silves signature), grilled meats, and local wines
meals.dinner: Private Fado dinner experience — a curated four-course dinner featuring regional dishes such as açorda de mariscos, slow-braised lamb, and almond tart, accompanied by live Fado performance and paired wines

day_by_day.notes: The Silves Medieval Fair takes place in August, but the castle is spectacular year-round. Book the Fado dinner experience well in advance as intimate performances have limited capacity.

day_by_day.morning: Full beach day at Praia da Marinha — your home beach and one of Portugal's most beautiful. Arrive early to secure the best spot. Swim in the crystal-clear water, snorkel around the rock formations, and simply relax on the golden sand. Arrange sun loungers and a parasol through the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the coastal walking trail from Praia da Marinha eastward toward Praia de Albandeira and Praia do Carvalho — a stunning 2-hour cliff-top walk with dramatic views, hidden beaches, and natural arches. The September light is golden and perfect for this walk.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset wine tasting on the hotel terrace — the sommelier or hotel staff curates a selection of six premium Portuguese wines (Alentejo, Algarve, Douro, and Vinho Verde) with paired nibbles as the sun sets over the Atlantic.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay
meals.lunch: Luxury beach picnic arranged by the hotel — chilled seafood, artisan sandwiches, local cheeses, fresh fruit, and a bottle of chilled Algarve white wine delivered to your beach spot
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Vila Joya in Albufeira (approximately 20 minutes east) — a legendary two-Michelin-starred restaurant considered one of Portugal's finest, with a breathtaking tasting menu and world-class wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: Vila Joya requires reservations well in advance — book as early as possible. The tasting menu at Vila Joya is a multi-hour culinary journey; plan for a late dinner. This is the premium dining highlight of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided jeep safari through the Algarve hinterland — explore the wild Serra de Monchique mountain range, passing through cork oak forests, carob groves, and traditional whitewashed villages. Visit a local medronho (arbutus berry brandy) distillery for a tasting of this unique Algarvian spirit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the spa town of Caldas de Monchique — a charming 19th-century thermal spa village nestled in a lush valley. Stroll through the leafy gardens, sample the famous mineral spring water, and browse artisan craft shops. Optional: book a thermal spa treatment at the historic Termas de Monchique.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel via the scenic mountain road with views over the entire Algarve coastline stretching to the Atlantic. Relaxed evening at the hotel with a nightcap on the terrace.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurante Central in Monchique town — a beloved mountain restaurant famous for its slow-roasted espetada (pork skewers), chouriço grilled on the table, and local red wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante O Leão de Porches in Porches — a sophisticated restaurant in a converted manor house specialising in elevated Algarvian cuisine with an outstanding wine list

day_by_day.notes: The Monchique mountains are noticeably cooler than the coast — bring a light layer. The jeep safari typically lasts 5-6 hours. Book in advance with a reputable operator offering private tours.

day_by_day.morning: Private yacht charter departing from Portimão Marina for a full-day luxury sailing experience along the Algarve's most spectacular coastline. The yacht heads west, passing Praia da Marinha, Benagil, Carvoeiro, and onward toward Ponta da Piedade in Lagos. Swim from the yacht in secluded coves accessible only by boat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the yacht journey — anchor in a private cove for a gourmet lunch on deck, snorkelling, and paddleboarding from the back of the boat. The crew serves chilled wines, fresh seafood, and canapés throughout the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Portimão Marina at sunset. Private transfer back to the hotel. Light evening at the property — perhaps a glass of wine on the terrace and an early night after a full day on the water.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay before departure to the marina
meals.lunch: Gourmet on-board lunch prepared by the yacht's crew — whole grilled sea bream, prawn and avocado salad, artisan breads, local cheeses, fresh fruit, and chilled Alvarinho wine
meals.dinner: Light dinner at the hotel or nearby — grilled fish of the day, salad, and a glass of local wine to end a relaxed day

day_by_day.notes: Book the private yacht charter at least one week in advance. Specify dietary preferences to the crew for the on-board lunch. Bring high-SPF sunscreen, a hat, and polarised sunglasses — September sun on the water is intense.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Porches Pottery studio and shop — one of the Algarve's most iconic artisan destinations, just minutes from the hotel. Watch master craftsmen hand-paint traditional blue-and-white azulejo-inspired ceramics. Browse and purchase premium pieces as unique souvenirs or gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming coastal village of Ferragudo — a picturesque fishing village across the Arade River from Portimão, largely untouched by mass tourism. Walk the cobbled streets, visit the 16th-century Castelo de São João do Arade, and enjoy the laid-back atmosphere of an authentic Algarvian village.
day_by_day.evening: Premium wine dinner at a renowned Algarve wine estate — return to Quinta dos Vales or visit Quinta da Penina for a private sunset dinner among the vines, with a sommelier-led pairing of their finest reserve wines with a four-course seasonal menu.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurante Sueste in Ferragudo — a riverside institution with exceptional fresh seafood, grilled fish, and a terrace overlooking the Arade River and Portimão skyline
meals.dinner: Private wine estate dinner — four-course seasonal menu with sommelier-led premium wine pairing at Quinta dos Vales or Quinta da Penina

day_by_day.notes: Porches Pottery is open Monday to Friday and Saturday mornings — confirm hours in advance. Ferragudo is best explored on foot. The private estate dinner should be booked several days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise yoga or meditation session on the cliff top above Praia da Marinha — arrange through the hotel with a private instructor. The golden September morning light over the Atlantic from this vantage point is extraordinary. Follow with a refreshing swim at the beach below.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Zoomarine theme park in Guia (approximately 20 minutes east) for a lighter, fun afternoon — or alternatively, explore the Aquashow water park. For a more culturally enriching option, visit the Museu Municipal de Loulé in Loulé town — the best local history museum in the central Algarve, housed in a restored Moorish castle.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-style premium dinner in Albufeira's marina area or at a top restaurant in the central Algarve — celebrating the penultimate full days of the trip with a special meal.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurante A Ruína in Albufeira — a legendary Algarvian institution built into the ruins of the old town walls, with spectacular sea views, fresh fish displays, and premium grilled seafood
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Henrique Leis in Almancil — a Michelin-starred restaurant in a converted Algarvian farmhouse, offering an extraordinary fusion tasting menu blending Brazilian and Portuguese influences with world-class wines

day_by_day.notes: Book Henrique Leis well in advance — it is one of the most sought-after restaurant reservations in the Algarve. The tasting menu is extensive; plan for a 3-hour dinner experience.

day_by_day.morning: Final beach morning at Praia da Marinha — a last swim in the turquoise waters, a cliff-top walk to say goodbye to the golden limestone scenery, and quiet time on the sand. Collect a few smooth pebbles or shells as natural mementos of this extraordinary coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Quinta do Lago or Vale do Lobo resort area in the Golden Triangle — the Algarve's most exclusive enclave. Browse the premium boutiques, enjoy a round of golf at one of the championship courses (optional, book in advance), or simply walk the boardwalk through the Ria Formosa Natural Park, a UNESCO-protected lagoon teeming with birdlife.
day_by_day.evening: Grand farewell dinner at one of the Algarve's most prestigious restaurants in the Golden Triangle — a fitting conclusion to a luxury trip.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay — request a special final-morning spread
meals.lunch: Lunch at Bovino Steakhouse at Quinta do Lago — a premium steakhouse and social club set in a stunning lakeside location, serving dry-aged prime beef, fresh seafood, and exceptional wines in a glamorous setting
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Gusto by Heinz Beck at Conrad Algarve in Almancil — a Michelin-starred restaurant helmed by one of Europe's most celebrated chefs, offering an exquisite Italian-Portuguese fusion tasting menu with a legendary wine programme

day_by_day.notes: Gusto by Heinz Beck requires advance reservations. The Golden Triangle area (Quinta do Lago, Vale do Lobo, Almancil) is approximately 40 minutes east of the hotel — arrange a private driver for the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Final leisurely morning at the boutique stay. Enjoy a long, relaxed gourmet breakfast on the terrace. Take a final walk along the cliff path above Praia da Marinha, breathing in the sea air and capturing last photographs of the iconic golden cliffs. Check out of the hotel at the agreed time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer to Faro Airport (approximately 45 minutes). Depending on your departure flight time, stop en route at a premium café in Almancil or Faro city for a farewell bica (espresso) and pastel de nata. Browse the airport's premium shops for last-minute Portuguese wine, olive oil, or artisan gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Faro Airport. Carry the memories of 13 extraordinary days on the Algarve coast.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay — a special spread requested in advance: smoked salmon, scrambled eggs, local cheeses, honey from the Algarve, freshly squeezed orange juice, and artisan pastries
meals.lunch: Light lunch or snacks at Faro Airport or en route — a premium café stop in Almancil for a final pastel de nata and coffee
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Confirm check-out time with the hotel the evening before. Request a packed lunch or snack bag from the hotel if the flight departs in the early afternoon. Allow 2 hours at Faro Airport for international departures. Consider shipping any wine purchases home through a specialist wine courier to avoid airline restrictions.
